pageDescription: How each part of the dashboard works.
dashboardsCardDescription: Build your own overview from widgets — clock, weather, calendar, and data from any section.
dashboardsIntroP1: Dashboards are named overview pages inside a workspace. Each one holds widgets: global ones (clock and date, weather, calendar, note) and ones that read a section — bookmarks, service status, server metrics, mail, alerts, and logs.
dashboardsIntroP2: Widgets sit on a 12-column grid and can be dragged and resized, but only in edit mode — in normal mode the tiles stay interactive and never move on a stray press. Widget data refreshes itself once a minute while the page is open. Dashboards are shared across the workspace, and one of them can be made the start page, which is what opens right after signing in.
dashboardsSteps: Choose “New dashboard” from the actions menu and give it a name — for example “Production” or “On call”.
Click “Edit”, then “Add widget”, and pick a type from the catalogue.
The widget's settings open right after it is added: that is where you set weather coordinates, a bookmark category, a specific server or mailbox, how many entries to show, and a custom title.
In edit mode, drag a widget by the handle on the left of its header, and resize it from the grip in the bottom-right corner — with the grip focused, the arrow keys resize it a cell at a time.
Click “Done” to leave edit mode: widgets then show a link into their section instead of the actions menu.
The dashboard menu renames it, makes it the start page, or deletes it — deleting a dashboard never touches section data.
bookmarksCardDescription: Organize saved links into categories and subcategories.
bookmarksIntroP1: Bookmarks stores links to sites and tools you use often, grouped into categories with one level of subcategories. Each bookmark can have a name, URL, description, and icon.
bookmarksIntroP2: Categories and bookmarks can be reordered by drag-and-drop, and the whole library can be searched or filtered by category.
bookmarksSteps: Click "New category" to create a top-level category, or add a subcategory from an existing category's menu.
Inside a category, click "Add" to create a bookmark with a name, URL, description, and icon.
Drag a category header or bookmark card to reorder it; drag a bookmark onto another category to move it there.
Use the search box to filter by name, description, or URL, and the category dropdown to show only one category.
Use a category's or bookmark's menu to rename or delete it — deleting a category also deletes its bookmarks.
domainsCardDescription: View and manage DNS records across connected providers.
domainsIntroP1: Domains lists every domain from your connected DNS providers (Cloudflare, Hetzner DNS, GoDaddy) in one table, with the number of DNS records and which provider manages it.
domainsIntroP2: From a domain you can drill into its DNS records, or link it to an existing Bookmark or Service — or create one pre-filled with the domain's name.
domainsSteps: Click "Add provider" to connect a Cloudflare, Hetzner DNS, or GoDaddy API credential.
The table lists every domain across providers, with its DNS record count and provider badge.
Click "View DNS records" on a domain to see and edit its DNS records.
Use the row's link menu to create or open a linked Bookmark or Service for that domain.
If a provider shows an error banner, click "Retry" to re-fetch it live.
serversCardDescription: Monitor and control servers from cloud providers and the metrics agent.
serversIntroP1: Servers shows every server from your connected cloud providers alongside any host running the InSpoter metrics agent, combined into one card per server.
serversIntroP2: Each card shows live status, CPU/RAM/disk usage, OS, location, and uptime, and — where the provider supports it — Start/Stop/Restart controls.
serversSteps: Click "Add provider" to connect a server-hosting provider credential.
Each card shows status, CPU/RAM/disk usage (from the metrics agent if installed, otherwise the provider's plan capacity), OS, location, and uptime.
Use the Start, Stop, or Restart buttons (with a confirmation dialog) to control provider-managed servers.
Click "Refresh" to force a live re-fetch of every provider instead of the cached snapshot.
For a server without live metrics, click "Set up monitoring" to enroll it with the metrics agent.
hostingCardDescription: Track shared hosting accounts across connected providers.
hostingIntroP1: Hosting aggregates shared-hosting/control-panel accounts from your connected providers into one card grid, showing domain, plan, and status.
hostingIntroP2: Each card reports disk and bandwidth usage, database and e-mail account counts, and — for supported providers — lets you suspend or unsuspend the account.
hostingSteps: Click "Add provider" to connect a hosting-panel API credential.
Each card shows the account's domain, status, disk and bandwidth usage with meters, database and e-mail counts, and plan.
Where supported, use Suspend/Unsuspend (with a confirmation dialog) to change the account's state.
Click "Refresh" to force a live re-fetch; a failing provider shows a retry banner.
servicesCardDescription: Uptime monitoring for HTTP, TCP, and PING targets.
servicesIntroP1: Services runs uptime checks against HTTP, TCP, or PING targets you define, polling on the interval you set and recording a status history for each.
servicesIntroP2: Every card auto-refreshes roughly every 10 seconds and shows the current status, last check time, response time, and a heartbeat strip of recent checks.
servicesSteps: Click "New service" to add an HTTP, TCP, or PING monitor with its target address and check interval.
Each card auto-refreshes and shows a status badge, last-checked time, response time, and a heartbeat strip of recent checks.
Click "Check now" to force an immediate check outside the regular interval.
Use Pause/Resume to stop or restart monitoring without deleting the service.
Use "Manage labels" to create labels, then the search box and label filter to narrow the list.
Click a card's title to open its detail page, or use the card menu to edit or delete it.
mailCardDescription: A three-pane webmail client for connected IMAP accounts.
mailIntroP1: Mail is a three-pane webmail client — accounts and folders on the left, the message list in the middle, and the reading pane on the right — for IMAP/SMTP mailboxes you connect, plus a built-in webhook mailbox for mail received over the API.
mailIntroP2: You can search, filter to unread, sort, reply/forward/archive/delete, apply labels, and set up filter rules that automatically label future incoming mail.
mailSteps: Click "Add account" to connect an IMAP/SMTP mailbox.
Pick an account and folder in the sidebar, then use search, "Unread only", and sort to narrow the message list.
Click a message to read it, and use Reply, Forward, Archive, Delete, or mark read/unread from the reading pane.
Click "Sync" to pull new mail from the server on demand.
Use "Manage labels" to create colored labels and apply them to messages, and "Filter rules" to auto-label future mail matching a sender or subject.
Click "Compose" to write new mail; unsent drafts are saved and reopened from the Drafts folder.
messagesCardDescription: Slack-style channels for internal chat and incoming webhooks.
messagesIntroP1: Messages organizes channels into categories, similar to Slack, for both manual team chat and messages posted in by external systems through a channel's webhook.
messagesIntroP2: Select a channel to see its timeline, scroll up to load older history, and send messages from the composer at the bottom.
messagesSteps: Use the sidebar's "+" controls to create a category, then a channel inside it.
Select a channel to view its message timeline; scroll up or click "Load previous" for older messages.
Type in the composer and send to post a message to the selected channel.
Open a channel's settings (gear icon) to rename it or manage its incoming webhook, used by external systems to post into it.
Use the category or channel context menu to rename or delete it.
activityCardDescription: Audit log of every action taken in the workspace.
activityIntroP1: Activity is a read-only audit trail of every create, update, delete, and other action operators take across the workspace — bookmarks, domains, servers, mail, tokens, and more.
activityIntroP2: Entries are searchable and filterable, and each row can be expanded to see the full details of what changed.
activitySteps: Use the search box, and the Action, Entity type, and Operator filters to narrow the table.
Use the sort control to switch between newest-first and oldest-first.
Click the chevron on a row with details to expand its full change payload.
Use Previous/Next to page through history.
logsCardDescription: Central log collector fed by the incoming webhook API.
logsIntroP1: Logs stores log lines pushed in by external systems through the log webhook endpoint, so scripts, cron jobs, and services outside InSpoter have one place to report what they did.
logsIntroP2: Entries are searchable and filterable by level and source, and each row can be expanded to see its full message and details.
logsSteps: Point an external system at the log webhook endpoint with a bearer token to start sending entries (see the example request shown when the list is empty).
Use the search box, Level filter, and Source filter to narrow the list.
Use the sort control to switch between newest-first and oldest-first.
Click the chevron on a row to expand its full message and details.
Use Previous/Next to page through results.
alertsCardDescription: Categorized alert inbox fed by the incoming webhook API.
alertsIntroP1: Alerts stores alert events pushed in by external systems through the alert webhook endpoint, organized into categories you define (e.g. "Deploy", "Security") with an info/warning/error/critical severity.
alertsIntroP2: Entries are searchable and filterable by category and severity, so you can triage what needs attention.
alertsSteps: Click "New category" to define alert categories used to classify incoming alerts.
Point an external system at the alert webhook endpoint with a bearer token, including category, severity, source, and message (see the example request shown when the list is empty).
Use the search box, Category filter, and Severity filter to narrow the table.
Use the sort control and Previous/Next to page through results.
Use "Manage categories" to rename or delete alert categories.
